subsystems.name: Flag qubits
subsystems.role: extra qubits that signal when a fault in the syndrome extraction circuit could cause a harmful error.

subsystems.name: Ancilla register
subsystems.role: qubits used to measure stabilizer operators without disturbing the logical data qubits.

subsystems.name: Syndrome extraction circuit
subsystems.role: the sequence of gates that entangles data, ancilla and flag qubits to extract error information.

subsystems.name: Classical decoder
subsystems.role: interprets syndrome and flag outcomes to identify the most likely error.

subsystems.name: Correction layer
subsystems.role: applies the physical operations that return the logical qubits to their intended state.

subsystems.name: Logical qubit register
subsystems.role: the protected quantum information that the protocol is meant to keep alive.

buildSteps.title: Choose a quantum error-correcting code
buildSteps.detail: Select a stabilizer code (e.g., surface or color code) whose logical qubits you want to protect, defining the stabilizer generators to be measured.

buildSteps.title: Design flag circuits
buildSteps.detail: For each stabilizer measurement, build a circuit that adds flag qubits and gate ordering so that any single fault that could propagate to a high-weight error flips at least one flag.

buildSteps.title: Prove fault tolerance on paper
buildSteps.detail: Enumerate all fault paths of weight up to the code's distance and verify that flagged faults are either correctable or lead to a safely repeatable measurement.

buildSteps.title: Map to quantum hardware
buildSteps.detail: Compile the abstract circuit onto a physical qubit connectivity graph, respecting native gate sets, measurement and reset capabilities.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate gates and measurements
buildSteps.detail: Tune control pulses so that single-qubit and two-qubit gate fidelities are high enough that faults are rare, and mid-circuit measurement is reliable.

buildSteps.title: Run syndrome extraction cycles
buildSteps.detail: Execute the flag circuits repeatedly, recording both stabilizer outcomes and flag outcomes for each cycle.

buildSteps.title: Decode with flag information
buildSteps.detail: Feed syndromes and flags to a classical decoder that treats flagged cycles as unreliable, either correcting based on the flag pattern or discarding and repeating that cycle.

buildSteps.title: Apply corrections and repeat
buildSteps.detail: Use the decoder output to apply physical corrections, then continue cycling to maintain the logical qubit over many error-correction rounds.

prerequisites.why: provides the stabilizer formalism and codes that flag protocols extend.
fault-tolerant thresholds require gate errors well below one percent, achieved in some small systems but not yet at scale.
flag and ancilla qubits must be measured and reused without disturbing data qubits.
decisions based on flags must be fast enough to keep pace with the quantum circuit.
a useful logical qubit needs many physical qubits wired and controlled together.

pathway.milestone: theoretical flag protocols and small-scale proof-of-principle demonstrations
pathway.unlocks: confidence that low-weight faults can be caught without full fault-tolerant overhead.

pathway.milestone: integration of flag-based syndrome extraction into repeated logical-qubit experiments
pathway.unlocks: measured logical error rates below the physical error rate for small codes.

pathway.milestone: real-time flag-aware decoding on a distance-3 code
pathway.unlocks: demonstration of a complete fault-tolerant cycle with flagged corrections.

pathway.milestone: scaling flag protocols to distance-5 and larger codes
pathway.unlocks: practical fault-tolerant quantum computing with many logical qubits.
